q: Which statement about the conversion of pyruvate to lactate is correct?
options: Pyruvate is oxidised and NAD+ is reduced, and one CO2 is released per pyruvate
Pyruvate is first decarboxylated to a 2C compound, which is then reduced to lactate
Pyruvate is reduced and NADH is oxidised; no CO2 is released
Lactate formation requires oxygen to act as the final hydrogen acceptor
explanation: Lactate (3C) has the same number of carbons as pyruvate (3C), so there is no decarboxylation – unlike yeast, where pyruvate → ethanal + CO2 → ethanol. Pyruvate acts as the hydrogen acceptor in place of O2: it is reduced, while NADH is oxidised back to NAD+.
